quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener is visibly skeptical of a new health-tech product and says nothing at all, just crosses their arms. What should the pitch do differently than usual?
quests.correctAnswer: Slow down and offer something small and verifiable first, rather than pushing forward with the full pitch at the same pace.
quests.hint: Silence and closed body language usually call for less pressure, not more enthusiasm.
quests.explanation: Reading non-verbal resistance matters as much as reading spoken objections - the response should be to ease off, not push harder.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Deliver a slower, lower-pressure opening for a blood-test platform, aimed at that visibly skeptical listener.
quests.correctAnswer: No pressure at all - would it help if I just showed you what the actual report looks like, rather than explaining it first?
quests.hint: Offer something concrete and low-commitment rather than continuing to explain in the abstract.
quests.explanation: Offering to show rather than tell can lower resistance in a way that more explanation, delivered at the same pace, usually can't.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The skeptical listener finally says 'I've just heard too many health claims that didn't hold up.' Respond honestly, acknowledging the pattern they're describing.
quests.correctAnswer: That's a completely fair thing to be tired of - we don't make any claim that isn't printed exactly as tested, nothing dressed up.
quests.hint: Validate the pattern they've experienced before making any further claim.
quests.explanation: Naming and validating a real pattern of past disappointment, before saying anything else, is often what finally earns a skeptical listener's attention.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener glances at their watch mid-pitch. What should the response prioritize: finishing the planned pitch, or adjusting to the visible time pressure?
quests.correctAnswer: Adjusting to the visible time pressure - continuing the original pitch unchanged ignores a clear signal the listener just gave.
quests.hint: A visible cue like checking the time is real information about what this listener needs right now.
quests.explanation: Noticing and responding to real-time cues, not just spoken objections, is part of reading resistance accurately.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Compress a teletherapy platform pitch down to its single strongest sentence, for the listener who just checked their watch.
quests.correctAnswer: Real quick - same-week appointments, not a month-long waitlist. Happy to say more later if that's useful.
quests.hint: Cut to the single strongest claim and offer to follow up rather than continuing at length.
quests.explanation: Compressing under a real-time cue, rather than a rehearsed level of detail, respects the listener's actual, visible constraint.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener says 'sorry, I really do have to run, but text me the info.' Deliver the one-line message you'd actually send afterward.
quests.correctAnswer: As promised - same-week appointments, no long waitlist. Here's the link if you want to take a look when you have a minute.
quests.hint: Keep the follow-up brief and consistent with what was said in person.
quests.explanation: A short, consistent follow-up message respects the rushed listener's time exactly as much as the compressed in-person pitch did.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener assumes your home-buying app is for real estate agents, not first-time buyers. What should the response do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Clarify who it's actually for, clearly and without making the listener feel silly for the mix-up.
quests.hint: A misdirected assumption about the audience needs a direct, friendly correction before anything else.
quests.explanation: An audience misunderstanding, left uncorrected, means the rest of the pitch will keep missing the actual point for this listener.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Correct that misunderstanding and re-pitch the home-buying app to the actual intended audience: first-time buyers overwhelmed by paperwork.
quests.correctAnswer: Actually, it's built for buyers, not agents - it translates all that confusing legal paperwork into plain language so a first-time buyer isn't lost in it.
quests.hint: Clarify the intended audience, then immediately re-deliver the pitch aimed correctly.
quests.explanation: Once the audience misunderstanding is corrected, the original pitch usually just needs to be re-aimed, not entirely rebuilt.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener, now understanding it's for buyers, says 'oh, I wish I'd had this last year - my sister's buying her first place now though.' Respond in a way that turns this into a useful next step.
quests.correctAnswer: That's exactly who this is for - want me to send you the link so you can pass it along to her?
quests.hint: Offer a concrete, low-pressure next step that fits the situation they just revealed.
quests.explanation: A cleared-up misunderstanding can open an unexpected but genuinely useful next step - staying alert to that is part of handling resistance well.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener assumes a free trial actually requires a credit card and long-term commitment, and hesitates because of that assumption. What should the response do?
quests.correctAnswer: Correct the specific factual misunderstanding plainly, since the hesitation is based on incorrect information, not a real objection.
quests.hint: This isn't a real objection to overcome - it's a factual error to correct.
quests.explanation: Some resistance isn't really resistance at all - it's a misunderstanding that dissolves the moment it's corrected.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Correct that misunderstanding for a meal-kit trial: no card required, no long-term commitment.
quests.correctAnswer: Actually no card needed at all for the trial, and there's nothing to cancel later if you don't love it - it just ends on its own.
quests.hint: State the actual terms plainly and specifically.
quests.explanation: A plain, specific correction of the actual terms usually resolves this kind of resistance faster than any additional persuasion would.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener, relieved, says 'oh, in that case, sure, why not.' Close warmly without oversell, matching their now-relaxed tone.
quests.correctAnswer: Great, I think you'll like it - and if you don't, no hard feelings, it just stops on its own.
quests.hint: Keep the close brief, warm, and low-pressure, matching the tone the listener just used.
quests.explanation: Matching the listener's newly relaxed tone, rather than escalating enthusiasm once they've agreed, keeps the close feeling natural.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener says 'I've tried things like this before and it just didn't work for me' about a fitness app, with a slightly discouraged tone. What should the response prioritize over persuasion?
quests.correctAnswer: Acknowledging the discouragement itself, briefly and genuinely, before making any further case for the product.
quests.hint: An emotional undertone deserves to be addressed before the logical objection is answered.
quests.explanation: When resistance carries real discouragement, acknowledging the feeling first - briefly, without dwelling - usually opens the door further than jumping straight to counter-arguments.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: After acknowledging the discouragement, offer a low-pressure, honest next step for that fitness app, rather than a big promise.
quests.correctAnswer: That's a really common feeling, and fair - no big promises from me, just: want to try one ten-minute session and see how it actually feels, no commitment beyond that?
quests.hint: Keep the ask small and low-pressure, matching the tone of someone who's been let down before.
quests.explanation: A small, low-pressure ask respects someone who's genuinely been disappointed before, rather than repeating the same size promise that let them down previously.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener agrees to try the one session and says 'okay, but if it's like the others, I'm done.' Respond honestly, without overpromising.
quests.correctAnswer: That's completely fair - I'd rather you judge it after actually trying it than take my word for it either way.
quests.hint: Accept their honest condition without over-reassuring or overselling.
quests.explanation: Letting the listener set their own terms for evaluation, without arguing against it, is a genuinely respectful way to handle lingering doubt.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A technically sophisticated listener challenges a specific claim: 'that response time seems unrealistic for that kind of query load.' What should the response avoid?
quests.correctAnswer: Vague reassurance without any real technical specificity - this listener will notice if the answer dodges the actual technical challenge.
quests.hint: This listener is asking a precise question and needs a precise answer.
quests.explanation: A technical challenge from a technical listener needs a technical answer - softening it into vague reassurance tends to lose credibility, not gain it.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Respond to that specific technical challenge with real specificity, for a database query tool.
quests.correctAnswer: Fair to question - that number's from caching common queries ahead of time, not from raw uncached lookups, which is a fair thing to clarify.
quests.hint: Give the actual technical reason behind the number, since this listener can follow it.
quests.explanation: Providing the real technical reasoning, rather than a general reassurance, is what actually satisfies a listener capable of evaluating it.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener says 'okay, that makes sense, but what about under a cache miss?' Answer that specific follow-up directly and honestly.
quests.correctAnswer: Slower on a cache miss, no argument there - though it's rare enough in typical usage that it's usually not the bottleneck people expect.
quests.hint: Answer honestly, including any real limitation, rather than avoiding the harder question.
quests.explanation: A direct, honest answer about a real limitation, once a technical listener asks outright, usually builds more trust than pretending the limitation doesn't exist.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener asks pointedly, 'what makes you qualified to be telling me this?' What tone should the response avoid?
quests.correctAnswer: Defensiveness or over-justification - a long list of credentials recited defensively can sound more insecure than confident.
quests.hint: The question is a direct challenge, and matching it with visible defensiveness tends to backfire.
quests.explanation: A calm, brief answer to a credibility challenge reads as more confident than an elaborate, defensive justification.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Answer 'what makes you qualified to be telling me this?' calmly and briefly, for a freelance nutrition coach.
quests.correctAnswer: Fair question - I've been doing this for six years, and honestly, most of what I know came from getting it wrong myself first.
quests.hint: Give a brief, honest, non-defensive answer.
quests.explanation: A short, honest answer - including an honest admission of past mistakes - often reads as more credible than a polished, defensive resume recitation.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener follows up: 'so you're not actually a licensed dietitian then?' Answer honestly, without overstating your credentials.
quests.correctAnswer: Correct, I'm not - I work alongside a licensed dietitian on anything medical, and I'm upfront about that with every client.
quests.hint: Be honest about the limits of your credentials rather than blurring the distinction.
quests.explanation: Being precise and honest about the actual limits of your qualifications, rather than blurring them, is what keeps credibility intact under direct scrutiny.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: After a pitch, the listener just says 'huh, okay' and nothing more. What's the risk of filling that silence with more selling?
quests.correctAnswer: It can come across as pushy or as not trusting the listener to process what's already been said.
quests.hint: Consider what over-filling a quiet moment signals about your own confidence in the pitch.
quests.explanation: A confident pitch can tolerate a quiet moment - rushing to fill silence with more selling often signals the opposite of confidence.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Respond to a non-committal 'huh, okay' in a way that invites genuine reaction without pressuring for one.
quests.correctAnswer: No pressure to have a reaction right now - happy to answer anything if something comes to mind later.
quests.hint: Give the listener space rather than pushing for an immediate response.
quests.explanation: Explicitly giving space, rather than demanding a reaction, often earns a more genuine response than pressing for one immediately would.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A few moments later, the same listener says 'actually, wait, how does the pricing work again?' Answer that follow-up clearly, picking up naturally from the earlier pause.
quests.correctAnswer: Sure - it's a flat monthly rate, no per-user fees on top, so it doesn't get more expensive as your team grows.
quests.hint: Answer clearly and naturally, as if continuing the same relaxed conversation.
quests.explanation: Genuine space, given without pressure, sometimes produces the actual follow-up question a pushier response would have prevented entirely.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener raises a genuinely valid limitation your product actually has. What's the strongest response, compared to deflecting or minimizing it?
quests.correctAnswer: Acknowledge the real limitation honestly, and if possible, explain what's being done about it or how it's currently managed.
quests.hint: A genuine limitation deserves a genuine acknowledgment, not a dismissal.
quests.explanation: Honestly acknowledging a real limitation, rather than deflecting, tends to build more trust than pretending every product is flawless.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener correctly points out that your ride-scheduling app doesn't yet support wheelchair-accessible vehicles in most areas. Respond honestly.
quests.correctAnswer: You're right, and that's a real gap right now - we're expanding accessible vehicle coverage, but I won't pretend it's everywhere yet.
quests.hint: Confirm the limitation honestly rather than overstating current capability.
quests.explanation: Confirming a real gap honestly, rather than overselling current capability, respects the listener enough to let them make an informed decision.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener appreciates the honesty and asks 'do you know when that'll change?' Answer as honestly as you actually can, without inventing a certain timeline.
quests.correctAnswer: I don't have an exact date I can promise you, but it's an active priority - I'd rather tell you that honestly than give you a date I'm not sure of.
quests.hint: Be honest about the uncertainty itself, rather than inventing false precision.
quests.explanation: Admitting genuine uncertainty, instead of fabricating a confident timeline, keeps the credibility earned by the earlier honest admission intact.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: A listener has raised skepticism, a misunderstanding, and now a direct challenge to credibility, all in one conversation. What should guide how the pitch has evolved by this point?
quests.correctAnswer: Everything actually learned about this specific listener during the conversation, not the original prepared opening line.
quests.hint: By this point in a real conversation, the pitch should already look different from where it started.
quests.explanation: A pitch that hasn't changed at all after several rounds of real resistance probably wasn't actually listening.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: Given everything learned in a long resistance-filled conversation about a home security system - cost-sensitive, distrustful of past salespeople, cares mainly about their elderly parent's safety - deliver the pitch that reflects all of that.
quests.correctAnswer: Given everything you've said, here's the honest version: this is about your mom being able to reach help fast if something happens, priced fairly, and I'd rather you talk to two other customers directly than take my word for any of it.
quests.hint: Synthesize every real thing learned - the emotional core, the price sensitivity, the trust issue - into one honest, specific pitch.
quests.explanation: Synthesizing everything learned across a whole resistant conversation into one honest, specific final pitch is the real capstone skill of handling resistance.

quests.instruction: Deliver the pitch before the lift opens.
quests.prompt: The listener says quietly, 'okay. I think I actually needed to hear that.' Close the conversation warmly and simply, without oversell.
quests.correctAnswer: Take your time deciding - I'm glad it actually made sense, and that's really all that matters to me here.
quests.hint: Keep the close simple, warm, and free of further pressure now that trust has been genuinely earned.
quests.explanation: The strongest possible close after real, sustained resistance is often the quietest one - no further pitching needed once trust has actually landed.
